title: Alcohol use disorder: severity and remission
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM code for the patient's alcohol use, if any is reportable.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for alcohol use disorder and general health maintenance.

HPI
The patient is a 73-year-old male who presents today for a scheduled follow-up regarding his history of alcohol use disorder, severe. He reports that he has been abstinent from alcohol for over a year. He describes his current status as being in sustained remission. He states that he feels stable and has not experienced any cravings or urges to drink. He denies any recent falls, changes in mood, or significant physical symptoms. He is here to monitor his progress and ensure continued stability.

Review of Systems
The patient reports no chest pain, shortness of breath, or palpitations. He denies recent fevers, chills, or night sweats. He denies any joint pain or muscle weakness. He reports no changes in bowel habits or urinary frequency. He denies any recent headaches or dizziness.

Social History
The patient is retired and lives with his wife. He enjoys gardening and watching television. He reports no current tobacco use.

Family History
Father died of a myocardial infarction at age 68. Mother died of natural causes at age 84. Siblings include one brother with hypertension.

Vitals
Blood Pressure: 132/84 mmHg
Heart Rate: 72 bpm
Respiratory Rate: 16 breaths/min
Temperature: 98.6 F
SpO2: 97% on room air
Weight: 185 lbs

Recent Labs
AST: 24 U/L
ALT: 22 U/L
GGT: 18 U/L
Glucose: 105 mg/dL
eGFR: 78 mL/min/1.73m2

Medication List
Multivitamin daily
Aspirin 81mg daily

Exam
General: The patient appears well-nourished and in no acute distress. Alert and oriented x3.
Skin: No rashes or lesions noted.
Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm. S1, S2 heard. No murmurs.
Respiratory: Lungs clear to auscultation bilaterally.
Abdominal: Soft, non-tender, non-distended. No organomegaly.
Neurological: Cranial nerves intact. Gait is steady. Strength 5/5 in all extremities.

Assessment
1. Alcohol use disorder, severe. The patient is currently in sustained remission with no reported use for over a year.

Plan
1. Continue current plan for alcohol use disorder, severe. Provide positive reinforcement for continued abstinence.
2. Encourage continued participation in community support groups.
3. Follow up in 3 months for continued monitoring of remission status.

Electronically signed, H. Tanaka, NP, 05/14/2026
explanations: Alcohol use disorder, moderate or severe, in remission: F10.21, alcohol dependence in remission (HCC 139).

distractors.why: Moderate or severe use disorder is dependence (F10.2-).
